scopeDecisions.decision: Closure is defined by these behavioral acceptance conditions, observed through the REST surface (Identity Toolkit and Secure Token) on the disposable Identity Platform sandbox, as for AUTH-ACCOUNT.

Client and Admin SDK paths (verifyIdToken, verifySessionCookie, checkRevoked, createCustomToken, client token refresh) belong to AUTH-CONFIG-SDK. Session cookies have no REST consumer, so their verification is SDK behavior; this parent observes their creation and contents.
Token use in Security Rules (request.auth) belongs to FS-RULES; Auth tokens, claims and revocation observed through Firestore belong to AUTH-FS-CROSS.
Tenant-scoped tokens (tenant custom tokens, the tenant_id claim, tenant session cookies) belong to AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING, as AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A8.

Custom-token signatures: production verifies RS256 against the issuing service account's Google-held keys. fireemu verifies against service-account public keys supplied in its configuration (auth.customTokenSigners) and then refuses damaged signatures, unknown signers and other projects' service accounts as production does; without that configuration it keeps accepting the unsigned tokens the Admin SDK mints in emulator mode. Key ids and signatures are compared by presence only, because the two sides never hold the same keys.
Token refusals after disable, delete and password change are counted once in AUTH-ACCOUNT (its scope decision A6); this parent references them and re-verifies them on its own final artifact.

Second-factor claims belong to AUTH-MFA, federated IdP sessions (signInWithIdp) to AUTH-FEDERATION and email-link sessions to AUTH-ACTION, following AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decisions A4 and A10 and the parent boundaries in the goal inventory.
scopeDecisions.decidedBy: agent (follows AUTH-ACCOUNT A4 and A10; owner may revise)

scopeDecisions.decision: Any HTTP 429 or quota refusal in this corpus is classified INDETERMINATE; quotas belong to AUTH-CONFIG-SDK, as AUTH-ACCOUNT scope decision A7.

conditions.note: ID token header shape and claim set issued by password sign-up and sign-in, anonymous, test-phone and custom-token sign-in, with profile fields and account custom claims.
What sign-up, password sign-in and custom-token sign-in return when returnSecureToken is omitted or false, and whether the returned token is honoured.

Secure Token refresh: response members, form and JSON bodies, refresh-token identity, auth_time preservation, iat advance, repeated exchange and profile changes reaching the refreshed token, for password, anonymous, phone and custom sessions.
Refusals of the refresh exchange: missing or wrong grant type, missing, malformed, truncated or foreign refresh tokens, missing or invalid API key.

Refusals of damaged ID tokens (garbage, empty, missing, flipped or stripped signature, alg none, changed payload, refresh token in place of an ID token) on lookup, update, delete and session-cookie creation.

validSince revocation: the same-second boundary pinned from the token's own auth_time, one second later, moved back, set in the future; ID token, refresh and session-cookie paths; custom-token sessions and Admin password replacement.

Custom-token sign-in that creates or reuses an account (scope decision A9 of AUTH-ACCOUNT), developer claims, refresh, uid length and characters, disabled accounts, claim-size boundary and the token's own time claims.

Custom-token refusals: another project's service account, damaged or absent signature, alg none, wrong audience, missing, empty or numeric uid, iss different from sub, malformed developer claims and every reserved claim name.
Account custom claims against custom-token developer claims of the same name, at sign-in, after the account claims change and after they are cleared, for custom and password sessions.
createSessionCookie validDuration: omitted, the 300 s and two-week bounds and one past each, zero, negative, numeric string, fractional and non-numeric values; cookie header and claims.

Session cookies from anonymous, phone and claim-carrying sessions, after the account claims change, for disabled and deleted accounts, without an ID token, with an API key instead of an owner credential, and a session cookie offered where an ID token is expected.
An ID token past its one-hour lifetime on lookup, update, delete and session-cookie creation, an expired custom token, and the refresh that still succeeds.
Token refusals after disable, delete and password change are counted once in AUTH-ACCOUNT (its scope decision A6) and re-verified here on this parent's final artifact.
Every AUTH-CREDENTIAL and AUTH-ACCOUNT row compared on one final artifact, with the Rust workspace tests of that source.
Independent clean-context closure and security review of the final artifact and evidence.
